name: jev-translations
description: Jev translation conformance cases. One question check becomes exactly one Jev question: named answers become Choice, explicit yes and no answers become Noul, and one ordered scale becomes Score. Each case pins the complete translated question, its canonical text, and its translation-domain content hash, together with the evidence state that the projected inputs produce. Every wrapper translates the same definitions into the same questions and the same hashes. The group is mandatory for the TypeScript SDK and for the later Python SDK, whose native adapter must pass the same cases.

provenance.shapes_from: the question declarations in dist/index.d.mts of the pinned version

mapping.rule: Named answers become Choice criteria. The criteria keys are exactly the declared answer labels and each value is the answer description.

One question with exactly the answers yes and no becomes Noul. The yes description maps to criteria.true and the no description to criteria.false. The noul value of the answer is the probability of yes.

One ordered scale becomes Score. The criteria tuple holds the level descriptions in the declared order, indexed from zero. The level names stay in the check meaning; the adapter maps reported positions back to names.

state_envelope: One fixed key evidence holds exactly the projected inputs that the using list names. The envelope frames every supplied value as untrusted evidence for the question, never as instructions.

cases.note: One categorical question with named answers becomes one Choice question. The instructions hold the question wording unchanged and the criteria hold every answer description keyed by label.

question.instructions: Does every material claim in the proposed message follow from the evidence?

criteria.supported: All claims are supported with appropriate certainty and attribution.
criteria.contradicted: A material claim conflicts with the supplied evidence.
criteria.incomplete: Support for a material claim is missing or ambiguous.
